title: 70th CCE Prelims (13 Dec 2024) · General Studies · Set G
subject: BPSC CCE PYQ
topic: Complete official question booklet of the BPSC Integrated 70th Combined Competitive Examination (Preliminary), General Studies, held on 13 December 2024 — 150 questions.
description: All 150 questions of booklet series G exactly as printed (English version), with answers from the BPSC final answer key released on 17 January 2025. This paper has four options per question; several questions use 'More than one of the above' as option D, printed that way in the booklet. BPSC deleted four questions in the final key (Q.48, Q.54, Q.56, Q.121); they are kept here, marked as dropped, and count as correct for everyone. This is the main 13 December 2024 paper, not the 4 January 2025 re-exam. Negative marking: 1/3 mark per wrong answer, as in the real exam. Use the 2-hour timer for a full mock.

questions.question:
[Q.1]
Dalton's atomic theory successfully explained
i. Law of conservation of mass.
ii. Law of constant composition.
iii. Law of radioactivity.
iv. Law of multiple proportion.
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Dalton's theory explained the laws of conservation of mass, constant (definite) composition and multiple proportions; it says nothing about radioactivity, which was discovered a century later.

questions.question:
[Q.2]
Which of the following is a technopolis?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Silicon Valley (California) is the classic technopolis, a region built around high-technology industry and research.

questions.question:
[Q.3]
Which of the following acid is secreted in the stomach?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The gastric glands (parietal/oxyntic cells) of the stomach secrete hydrochloric acid, which activates pepsin and kills microbes.

questions.question:
[Q.4]
Which of the following ruler ruled Assam in the time of Harsha?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Bhaskaravarman of the Varman dynasty of Kamarupa (Assam) was Harsha's contemporary and ally; Hiuen Tsang visited his court.

questions.question:
[Q.5]
When was the undersea cable-based Chennai-Andaman and Nicobar (CANI) Project inaugurated and dedicated to the nation by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. PM Modi inaugurated the Chennai–Andaman & Nicobar Islands submarine optical fibre cable on 10 August 2020.

questions.question:
[Q.6]
The meter that is used to measure the distance moved by the vehicle is known as
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. An odometer records the distance travelled by a vehicle; a speedometer shows its instantaneous speed.

questions.question:
[Q.7]
Which Amendment to the Constitution abolished the two seats that were reserved for the Anglo-Indian community?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The 104th Amendment Act, 2019 ended the nomination of two Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha (and to State Assemblies) while extending SC/ST reservation.

questions.question:
[Q.8]
What should come in place of question mark (?) in the following?
[Figure: three X-shaped figures, each made of two crossed ovals with a number in each of the four arms and one number in the centre. Figure 1: top-left 16, top-right 21, bottom-left 15, bottom-right 10, centre 36. Figure 2: top-left 7, top-right 10, bottom-left 13, bottom-right 10, centre 16. Figure 3: top-left 15, top-right ?, bottom-left 21, bottom-right 14, centre 64.]
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The official key gives 22. BPSC did not publish the rule behind this figure puzzle.

questions.question:
[Q.9]
Which of the following ports is an artificial port?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Chennai harbour is an artificial harbour built in open sea with breakwaters; Mumbai, Kochi and Marmugao are natural harbours.

questions.question:
[Q.10]
In April 2024, how many members of the UN Security Council either rejected or abstained from voting for the proposal to allow Palestine to become a full member of the UN?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. On 18 April 2024 the UNSC draft got 12 votes in favour; the USA vetoed it and the UK and Switzerland abstained, so 3 members either rejected or abstained.

questions.question:
[Q.11]
In the Union Budget speech for 2024-25, which oilseeds were noted as not being covered under the goal of 'Atmanirbharta' (self-reliance) for oil?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. The 2024-25 Budget's strategy for self-reliance in oilseeds named mustard, groundnut, sesame, soybean and sunflower; coconut was not in the list.

questions.question:
[Q.12]
Sheikh Ahmad Abdullah al-Ahmad al Sabah was appointed as the new Prime Minister of which country in April 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Sheikh Ahmad Abdullah al-Ahmad al-Sabah was named Prime Minister of Kuwait in April 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.13]
Match the following in context of Asht Pradhan system of Maratha rulers:
Official — Department
a. Sachiva — 1. Prime Minister
b. Peshwa — 2. Incharge of Correspondence
c. Samant — 3. Finance Minister
d. Amatya — 4. Foreign Minister
Choose the correct option:
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. In the Ashtapradhan: Sachiv handled royal correspondence, Peshwa was the Prime Minister, Sumant/Samant was the foreign minister and Amatya was the finance minister, which gives a-2, b-1, c-4, d-3.

questions.question:
[Q.14]
According to the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) data from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, which indices experienced significant growth in Financial Year 2023?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. In FY 2022-23 the IIP use-based indices showing the strongest growth were capital goods and infrastructure/construction goods.

questions.question:
[Q.15]
Heat transfer that does not require a medium is called
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Radiation transfers heat as electromagnetic waves and needs no medium; this is how sunlight reaches Earth through space.

questions.question:
[Q.16]
Which type of rock is formed from cooling and solidification of lava?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Igneous rocks form when magma or lava cools and solidifies; extrusive (volcanic) rocks like basalt form from lava.

questions.question:
[Q.17]
After elections to the 18th Lok Sabha, who was appointed as the Union Minister of Textiles in the Modi government?
options: Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh (Munger)
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. In the third Modi government (June 2024), Giriraj Singh (Begusarai) became Union Minister of Textiles.

questions.question:
[Q.18]
Which of the following human races inhabitates in China, Mangolia and Japan?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. China, Mongolia and Japan are inhabited mainly by the Mongoloid race.

questions.question:
[Q.19]
"Chach Nama" was translated to Persian by
options: Muhammad Ali Bin Abu Bakr Kufi
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Chach Nama, the history of the Arab conquest of Sindh, was translated from Arabic into Persian by Muhammad Ali bin Hamid bin Abu Bakr Kufi in the early 13th century.

questions.question:
[Q.20]
Which of the following represent the suitable condition for the liquefaction of gases?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Gases liquefy more easily at low temperature (below their critical temperature) and high pressure, which bring the molecules close together.

questions.question:
[Q.21]
Name the constituency from where the new Chief Minister of Odisha, Mohan Charan Majhi was elected in the recent State Assembly elections.
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Mohan Charan Majhi won the Keonjhar Assembly seat in 2024 and became Chief Minister of Odisha.

questions.question:
[Q.22]
To highlight the hardships faced by the peasants, Sahajanand Saraswati published which newspaper?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Swami Sahajanand Saraswati, leader of the Kisan Sabha movement in Bihar, published the Hindi weekly 'Lok Sangraha' to highlight peasants' hardships.

questions.question:
[Q.23]
How many times do the hands of a clock coincide in a day?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. In 12 hours the hands coincide 11 times, so in 24 hours they coincide 22 times.

questions.question:
[Q.24]
Which of the following is an iron ore?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Limonite (hydrated iron oxide) is an iron ore; cinnabar is mercury ore, bauxite is aluminium ore, and pyrite (iron sulphide) is not mined as an iron ore.

questions.question:
[Q.25]
Who was the founder of the Farazi Movement?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The Faraizi movement in Bengal was founded by Haji Shariatullah in the early 19th century; his son Dudu Miyan led it later.

questions.question:
[Q.26]
Where was the top leader of Hamas, Ismail Haniyeh, assassinated on 31st July 2024, allegedly in an Israeli airstrike?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Ismail Haniyeh was assassinated in Tehran, Iran, on 31 July 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.27]
According to a CRISIL Rating report, how much is the corporate bond market expected to grow by Financial Year 2030 in India?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. A CRISIL Ratings report projected that India's corporate bond market would roughly double to ₹100–120 lakh crore by FY2030.

questions.question:
[Q.28]
Following are the mountain ranges of India
1. Garo Hills
2. Nandadevi
3. Kamet
4. K2
Which of the following is their correct sequence from east to west?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. From east to west: Garo Hills (Meghalaya), Nanda Devi (about 79.97°E), Kamet (about 79.59°E) and K2 (about 76.5°E), so 1-2-3-4.

questions.question:
[Q.29]
Match List – I with List – II:
List – I
a. Vaishali
b. Bhagalpur
c. Jamui
d. Madhepura
List – II
1. Silk Textile
2. Gold
3. Rail coach factory
4. Flori culture
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
a b c d
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. According to the key: Vaishali – floriculture (4), Bhagalpur – silk textile (1), Jamui – gold (2) and Madhepura – rail locomotive/coach factory (3).

questions.question:
[Q.30]
After remaining neutral for almost 200 years, which one of the following countries officially joined the NATO in March 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Sweden formally joined NATO on 7 March 2024 as its 32nd member, ending about 200 years of military non-alignment.

questions.question:
[Q.31]
Which component of fertilizer is used for stimulating early growth purpose?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Phosphorus promotes early root development and early growth of plants.

questions.question:
[Q.32]
Malik Kafur also known as "Hazar Dinari" was bought by whom?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Malik Kafur was bought for 1,000 dinars (hence 'Hazar Dinari') by Nusrat Khan, Alauddin Khilji's general, during the Gujarat campaign of 1299.

questions.question:
[Q.33]
In which of the following years the Bihar state Hydroelectric power corporation was established?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. The Bihar State Hydroelectric Power Corporation (BHPC) was set up in 1982.

questions.question:
[Q.34]
Who wrote "New Lamps For The Old"?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. 'New Lamps for Old' was a series of articles by Aurobindo Ghosh in the Indu Prakash (1893-94) criticising the moderate Congress.

questions.question:
[Q.35]
What was the theme of the International Olympic Day 2024 which is celebrated every year on 23rd June?
options: "Move, learn, discover – Together for a better world"
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The theme of Olympic Day 2024 (23 June) was 'Let's Move and Celebrate'.

questions.question:
[Q.36]
Who was the President of the Indian National Congress at Patna Session held in 1912?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The 27th INC session at Bankipore (Patna) in 1912 was presided over by R. N. Mudholkar.

questions.question:
[Q.37]
What is the 14th term of the sequence 14, 10, 6, 2,.... ?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. It is an arithmetic progression with a = 14 and d = –4, so T14 = 14 + 13 × (–4) = –38.

questions.question:
[Q.38]
What were the shares of the Agriculture, Industry and Services sectors in overall GVA at current prices in Financial Year 2024 according to the Economic Survey 2023-24?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. According to the Economic Survey 2023-24, the shares in GVA at current prices for FY24 were about 17.7% for agriculture, 27.6% for industry and 54.7% for services.

questions.question:
[Q.39]
In which city of Bihar the recently inaugurated National Dolphin Research Centre is located?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. India's (and Asia's) first National Dolphin Research Centre was inaugurated in Patna, on the bank of the Ganga, in 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.40]
Which of the following are the constituents of a soda acid fire extinguisher?
options: Conc. sulphuric acid and aluminium sulphate
Dil. sulphuric acid and sodium carbonate
Dil. sulphuric acid and sodium bicarbonate solution
Conc. sulphuric acid and sodium carbonate solution
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. A soda-acid extinguisher mixes dilute sulphuric acid with sodium bicarbonate solution, which produces CO2 under pressure.

questions.question:
[Q.41]
Which of the following bacterial disease that is called as spleenic fever?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Anthrax, caused by Bacillus anthracis, is also called splenic fever.

questions.question:
[Q.42]
Where was the Japan-India bilateral Maritime Exercise (JIMEX-24) held this year?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. JIMEX-24, the Japan-India maritime exercise, was held at Yokosuka, Japan, in June 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.43]
Ramkrishna Mission was founded by
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 (1 May 1897).

questions.question:
[Q.44]
In a certain code language COMPUTER is written as RFUVQNPC. How will MEDICINE be written in that code language?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. COMPUTER is reversed (RETUPMOC), the first and last letters are kept and every middle letter is moved +1, giving RFUVQNPC. MEDICINE reversed is ENICIDEM, which gives E-OJDJEF-M = EOJDJEFM.

questions.question:
[Q.45]
Which of the following radiation is used to get relief from body aches?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Infra-red radiation gives heat that penetrates tissue, so it is used in heat therapy to relieve body aches.

questions.question:
[Q.46]
Which of the following was the capital of Chera dynasty?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The early Chera capital was Vanji, identified with Karur (Karuvur) in Tamil Nadu.

questions.question:
[Q.47]
The book critical of the British Policies Gharib Hindustan was banned in Bihar in 1930 by the British was written by
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. According to the official key, the banned book 'Gharib Hindustan' was written by Mohd. Wali Hassan.

questions.question:
[Q.48]
What is the contribution of agriculture in the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): Deleted. Deleted by BPSC in the final answer key; counts as correct for everyone. Reason given by BPSC: the reference year is not mentioned in the question. (The provisional key had D, 26%.)

questions.question:
[Q.49]
By how much did the Female Labour Force Participation Rate increase from 2017-18 to 2022-23, according to the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. PLFS (NSSO) data show female LFPR rose from 23.3% in 2017-18 to 37.0% in 2022-23.

questions.question:
[Q.50]
Which country took over the chairmanship of BRICS on January 1, 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Russia took over the BRICS chairship on 1 January 2024 and hosted the Kazan summit.

questions.question:
[Q.51]
Which one of the following is an example of melamine used for making floor tiles?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Melamine (melamine-formaldehyde) is a thermosetting plastic; it does not soften on heating, so it suits floor tiles, kitchenware and fire-resistant fabrics.

questions.question:
[Q.52]
How many triangles are there in the following figure PQRS?
[Figure: rectangle PQRS with P top-left, Q top-right, R bottom-right and S bottom-left. Both diagonals PR and QS are drawn and cross at the centre O. A horizontal line runs from the midpoint of the left side PS to O, and a vertical line runs from O down to the midpoint of the bottom side SR.]
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The six smallest triangles are PMO, MSO, SNO, NRO, ORQ and OQP. Add PSO and SRO, and the four large triangles PQS, QRS, PQR and PSR. Total 12.

questions.question:
[Q.53]
Which of the following is a cause of rural to urban migration in India?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Cities' demand for labour, unbalanced rural-urban development and lack of rural jobs all drive rural-to-urban migration, so all the above.

questions.question:
[Q.54]
According to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), what is the forecast for headline inflation in Financial Year 2025?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): Deleted. Deleted by BPSC in the final answer key; counts as correct for everyone. Reason given by BPSC: RBI revises the projection every quarter, and the revised estimate on 6 December 2024 was 4.8%, which is not among the options. (The provisional key had D, 4.5%.)

questions.question:
[Q.55]
The hundred years of Indian National Congress in Bihar was edited by
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. According to the official key, 'The Hundred Years of Indian National Congress in Bihar' was edited by P. N. Ojha.

questions.question:
[Q.56]
In which organisms does spore formation occur as a mode of reproduction?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): Deleted. Deleted by BPSC in the final answer key; counts as correct for everyone. Reason given by BPSC: spore formation occurs in algae, fungi and ferns, so more than one option is correct. (The provisional key had D, Fern.)

questions.question:
[Q.57]
When did Britishers shifted the capital to Delhi?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The transfer of the capital was announced at the Delhi Durbar in December 1911 and took effect in 1912 (Delhi became capital on 1 April 1912), which is the key's answer. Note: some sources give 1911, the year of the announcement.

questions.question:
[Q.58]
Zoji-la Tunnel will connect which of the following places?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. The Zojila tunnel on NH-1 will give all-weather connectivity between Srinagar (Kashmir valley) and Leh (Ladakh).

questions.question:
[Q.59]
Who is the author of the autobiography "I Have the Streets : A Kutti Cricket Story"?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. 'I Have the Streets: A Kutti Cricket Story' (2024) is the memoir of R. Ashwin, written with journalist Sidharth Monga.

questions.question:
[Q.60]
Where was the 13th Ministerial Conference of World Trade Organization (WTO) held in February 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. The WTO's 13th Ministerial Conference (MC13) was held in Abu Dhabi, UAE, from 26 Feb to 2 Mar 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.61]
Which one of the following rivers is different from the others?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. The Narmada flows west into the Arabian Sea; the Tungabhadra, Penganga and Mahanadi systems all drain east to the Bay of Bengal.

questions.question:
[Q.62]
If ÷ means +, – means ÷, × means – and + means ×, then the value of
[(36 × 4) – 8 × 4] / [4 + 8 × 2 + 16 ÷ 1]
is
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. After swapping the signs, the expression becomes [(36 – 4) ÷ 8 – 4] / [4 × 8 – 2 × 16 + 1] = (4 – 4)/(32 – 32 + 1) = 0/1 = 0.

questions.question:
[Q.63]
Which of the following is the first artificially prepared element?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Technetium (Tc, Z = 43), made in 1937, was the first artificially produced element.

questions.question:
[Q.64]
What is the full form of CGTMSE?
options: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Macro and Small Enterprises
Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Medium and Small Enterprises
Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Medium Enterprises
Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. CGTMSE is the Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises, set up by the Ministry of MSME and SIDBI.

questions.question:
[Q.65]
Who gave the slogan "DO OR DIE" and when?
options: Subhash Chandra Bose during Quit India Movement
Jawahar Lal Nehru during Non-cooperation Movement
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Gandhiji gave the call 'Do or Die' on 8 August 1942 at the launch of the Quit India Movement.

questions.question:
[Q.66]
Which of the following is the fluid part of the blood?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Plasma is the fluid part of blood (about 55%); RBCs, WBCs and platelets are the formed elements.

questions.question:
[Q.67]
Consider the following about Ajivika sect:
a. Makhali Gosala was its most important leader.
b. Central idea of the philosophy was "NIYATI" that is fate.
c. The discrimination on the basis of caste and class.
d. The Ajivikas had regular sabhas for meetings.
options: b, c and d are correct
a, b and d are correct
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Makkhali Gosala led the Ajivikas, whose central idea was niyati (fate), and the sect held regular sabhas. So a, b and d are correct.

questions.question:
[Q.68]
Which of the following minerals occurs in the Minas Gerais province of Brazil?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Minas Gerais in Brazil is famous for its iron ore (e.g. Itabira).

questions.question:
[Q.69]
The first Hindi daily newspaper to be published in Bihar was
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. According to the official key, the first Hindi daily newspaper of Bihar was 'Sarva Hitaishi'.

questions.question:
[Q.70]
Which of the following has highly elongated elliptical orbit?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Comets move in highly elongated elliptical orbits around the Sun.

questions.question:
[Q.71]
If February 1, 1996 is Wednesday, what day is March 3, 1996?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. 1996 is a leap year: from 1 Feb to 3 Mar is 29 + 2 = 31 days, which is 3 odd days. Wednesday + 3 = Saturday.

questions.question:
[Q.72]
Name the place where Donald Trump was speaking at an election rally when an alleged Shooter, Thomas Matthew Crooks, shot and injured him.
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Trump was shot at a rally near Butler, Pennsylvania, on 13 July 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.73]
What is the position of India in manufacturing of mobile phones in 2023?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. India is the world's second largest manufacturer of mobile phones, after China.

questions.question:
[Q.74]
Which of the following cities is located along the side of river Seine?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Paris stands on the Seine; Belgrade and Budapest are on the Danube and Lisbon on the Tagus.

questions.question:
[Q.75]
According to the Reserve Bank of India, what is one of the eligibility criteria for a Small Finance Bank (SFB) to transition into a Universal Bank?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. RBI's 2024 guidelines require a Small Finance Bank wishing to become a universal bank to have a minimum net worth of ₹1,000 crore, among other criteria.

questions.question:
[Q.76]
Match the List – I with List – II and choose the correct answer:
List – I (Organization)
I. Swadeshi Sevak Home
II. United India House
III. Yugantar Ashram
IV. INA or Azad Hind Fauj
List – II (Headquarter)
a. Vancouver
b. Seattle
c. San Francisco
d. Rangoon
options: I – d, II – c, III – a, IV – b
I – d, II – c, III – b, IV – a
I – c, II – d, III – a, IV – b
I – a, II – b, III – c, IV – d
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Swadeshi Sevak Home was in Vancouver, United India House in Seattle and Yugantar Ashram (Ghadar) in San Francisco, and the INA was headquartered at Rangoon, so I-a, II-b, III-c, IV-d.

questions.question:
[Q.77]
When did Muslim League observed "Direct Action Day"?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. The Muslim League observed Direct Action Day on 16 August 1946; the Calcutta riots followed.

questions.question:
[Q.78]
In June 2024, which city was named India's "First UNESCO City of Literature"?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Kozhikode (Kerala) was declared India's first UNESCO 'City of Literature' on 23 June 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.79]
What is the structural and functional unit of life?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life.

questions.question:
[Q.80]
Gaurav walks 20 metres towards North. He then turns left and walks 40 metres. He again turns left and walks 20 metres. Further, he moves 20 metres after turning to the right. How far is he from his original position?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. North 20, left (west) 40, left (south) 20 brings him back to the starting latitude 40 m west; turning right (west) 20 more puts him 60 m from the start.

questions.question:
[Q.81]
Which one is not included in the Budget Priorities in pursuit of 'Vikasit Bharat' in Union Budget 2024-25?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. The nine budget priorities of 2024-25 include agriculture productivity, employment and skilling and energy security, but not 'Sustainable Development' as a separate priority.

questions.question:
[Q.82]
Which of the following drainage systems drains the lands of Bihar?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The Ghaghara (Ghagra) flows through north Bihar and joins the Ganga near Chhapra; the Mahanadi, Yamuna and Narmada do not drain Bihar.

questions.question:
[Q.83]
Consider the types of land according to The Amarkosha:
a. Urvara-fertile
b. Maru-desert
c. Shadvala-grassy
d. Devmatrika-watered by rain
Which of the following is correct?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The Amarakosha lists land types such as urvara (fertile), maru (desert), shadvala (grassy) and devamatrika (rain-fed), so more than one of the listed options is correct.

questions.question:
[Q.84]
Under Article "243J" which of the following can make provisions to the maintenance of accounts by Panchayats?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Article 243J: the State Legislature may by law provide for the maintenance of accounts by Panchayats and for their audit.

questions.question:
[Q.85]
Which of the following is a non-contact force?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Magnetic force acts without physical contact; friction and impact forces need contact.

questions.question:
[Q.86]
Motorcycle is related to battery in the same way as Life is related to
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. A motorcycle's battery supplies its energy just as the Sun is the source of energy for life on Earth.

questions.question:
[Q.87]
Consider the following about the King "Praversena":
a. He was the real founder of Vakataka dynasty.
b. His empire extended from Bundelkhand in north to Hyderabad in South.
c. He succeeded his father king Vindhyshakti.
d. He is mentioned in Puranas.
Which of the following statements are correct?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Pravarasena I is regarded as the real founder of the Vakataka power, succeeded his father Vindhyashakti and is mentioned in the Puranas; more than one of the given combinations fits.

questions.question:
[Q.88]
Match the following and choose the correct answer.
Newspaper — Editor
I. Free Hindustan — a. Mahatma Gandhi
II. Indian Opinion — b. Dadabhai Nauroji
III. Voice of India — c. Surendranath Banerjee
IV. Bengalee — d. Taraknath Das
options: I – c, II – d, III – a, IV – b
I – d, II – a, III – b, IV – c
I – c, II – a, III – d, IV – b
I – d, II – c, III – b, IV – a
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Free Hindustan – Taraknath Das, Indian Opinion – Mahatma Gandhi, Voice of India – Dadabhai Naoroji, Bengalee – Surendranath Banerjee.

questions.question:
[Q.89]
In which one of the following Freestyle weight categories, Aman Sehrawat became the first Indian male wrestler to qualify for the 2024 Paris Olympics at the World Wrestling Olympic Qualifiers, Turkiye in May 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Aman Sehrawat qualified in men's freestyle 57 kg at the World Olympic Qualifier in Istanbul (May 2024) and later won bronze at Paris.

questions.question:
[Q.90]
Which of the following districts of Bihar has the highest percentage of Scheduled Tribe population in 2011 census?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. According to Census 2011, Katihar has the highest proportion of Scheduled Tribe population among Bihar's districts (about 5.9%).

questions.question:
[Q.91]
Which sector received the highest allocation in the Bihar Budget 2024-25?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Education received the largest allocation in the Bihar Budget 2024-25.

questions.question:
[Q.92]
Choose the group of letters which is different from others.
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. ORUX, CFIL and JMPS each move +3, +3, +3; PSVX moves +3, +3, +2, so it is the odd one out.

questions.question:
[Q.93]
Which of the following corundum and cryolite are important ores?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Corundum (Al2O3) and cryolite (Na3AlF6) are aluminium minerals; cryolite is used as a flux in aluminium extraction.

questions.question:
[Q.94]
What is the eligibility age, after the changes made in March 2024, for senior citizens to vote by postal ballot?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. In March 2024 the age for home voting / postal ballot for senior citizens was raised from 80 to 85 years.

questions.question:
[Q.95]
In which of the following states of India has major reserves of coal?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh hold the largest coal reserves in India, so all the above.

questions.question:
[Q.96]
Which two words have been incorporated in the Preamble by 42nd Amendment?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble; of the pairs given, secular and socialist.

questions.question:
[Q.97]
In which Lok Sabha seat, one of India's Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), Shompen tribe, for the first time exercised their democratic right to vote in April 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The Shompen of Great Nicobar voted for the first time in April 2024 in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Lok Sabha seat.

questions.question:
[Q.98]
What was the Per Capita Net State Domestic Product at Current Prices for Bihar for the fiscal year 2022-23, based on the base year 2011-12?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. According to the official key, Bihar's per capita NSDP at current prices for 2022-23 (base 2011-12) was ₹54,111.

questions.question:
[Q.99]
Which of the following centres in Bihar is proposed to develop under Vishnupad Yojana for promotion of tourism in Union Budget 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The Union Budget 2024-25 announced corridors for the Vishnupad temple at Gaya (and the Mahabodhi temple at Bodh Gaya).

questions.question:
[Q.100]
Match the following and choose the correct answer.
Political Organisation — Founder
I. Khaksars — a. Subhash Chandra Bose
II. Socialist Party — b. Inayatullah Mashriqui
III. Independent Labour Party — c. Jayaprakash Narayan
IV. Forward Bloc — d. B. R. Ambedkar
options: I – b, II – d, III – a, IV – c
I – b, II – c, III – d, IV – a
I – c, II – d, III – a, IV – b
I – d, II – c, III – b, IV – a
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Khaksars – Inayatullah Mashriqi, Congress Socialist Party – Jayaprakash Narayan, Independent Labour Party – B. R. Ambedkar, Forward Bloc – Subhas Chandra Bose.

questions.question:
[Q.101]
Before his appointment as a judge of the Supreme Court of India in July 2024, Justice N. Kotiswar Singh was the Chief Justice of which High Court?
options: Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh High Court
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Justice N. Kotiswar Singh was Chief Justice of the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court before he was elevated to the Supreme Court in July 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.102]
The sikh pilgrimage site "TAKHAT SRI HARIMANDIR JI PATNA SAHIB" which is considered as the second holiest Takhat is located at
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Takht Sri Harimandir Ji Patna Sahib, the birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh, is in Patna.

questions.question:
[Q.103]
Bihula Festival is celebrated especially in which one of the following districts in Bihar usually in the month of August each year?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Bihula (Bishahari puja) is celebrated mainly in Bhagalpur, in the Anga region, in August.

questions.question:
[Q.104]
Which of the following is the resistance of the wire?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. By Ohm's law R = V/I.

questions.question:
[Q.105]
Which Article of the Constitution restrict a Member of Parliament to hold the office of profit?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Article 102(1)(a) disqualifies a person from Parliament if he holds an office of profit under the Government of India or a State.

questions.question:
[Q.106]
Which of the following great ruler founded the "Haryak Vansh" in ancient Bihar?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Bimbisara founded the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha (c. 544 BCE).

questions.question:
[Q.107]
Which one of the following is about Ruchira Kamboj, who was the first woman to become the Indian Ambassador to the United Nations who retired recently, is true?
options: She was a member of the NITI Ayog
She was a member of Indian Council of World Affairs
She held the position of Permanent Representative of India to UNESCO-Paris
She was the first woman Indian Ambassador to USA
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Ruchira Kamboj earlier served as India's Permanent Representative to UNESCO in Paris.

questions.question:
[Q.108]
Which of the following are exothermic processes?
i. Evaporation of water.
ii. Dilution of an acid (H₂SO₄).
iii. Reaction of water with quick lime.
iv. Sublimation of camphor (crystals).
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Dilution of H2SO4 and the reaction of quicklime with water release heat; evaporation and sublimation absorb heat.

questions.question:
[Q.109]
What is the object of "cut motion" in Parliament?
options: To move a proposal to reduce expenditure in the budget proposals
To restrict day-to-day financial expenditure of the government
To restrict grants from consolidated fund of India
To restrict the grants of the Government
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. A cut motion is moved to reduce the amount of a demand for grant in the budget.

questions.question:
[Q.110]
Who presented the Bihar Budget 2024-25 in the State Assembly?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Deputy CM and Finance Minister Samrat Choudhary presented the Bihar Budget 2024-25.

questions.question:
[Q.111]
When did the new province Bihar came into force during British rule?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The new province of Bihar and Orissa came into existence on 1 April 1912.

questions.question:
[Q.112]
Who headed the Royal Commission on Indian currency appointed in 1913?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. The Royal Commission on Indian Finance and Currency (1913) was chaired by Sir Austen Chamberlain; J. M. Keynes was a member.

questions.question:
[Q.113]
Which of the following is the value of solar constant?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. The solar constant is about 1.36–1.4 kW/m² (roughly 1361 W/m²).

questions.question:
[Q.114]
Which of the following was not one of the features of the Government of India Act, 1935?
options: Reconstruction of the Governor-General's Executive Council
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. 'Appraisal of the Act of 1935' is not a feature of the Act; provincial autonomy, the proposed All-India Federation and the changes to the Governor-General's council were.

questions.question:
[Q.115]
What is the position of representation of Anglo-Indian Community in Lok Sabha?
options: Nomination of them has been done away with by 104th Constitutional Amendment
Two anglo-Indians are nominated by the President
They are nominated as per their population
One anglo-Indian is nominated by the President
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The 104th Amendment (2019) did away with the nomination of Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha.

questions.question:
[Q.116]
Which community was categorized as Scheduled Caste (SC) by a 2015 Bihar government notification which was quashed in July 2024 by the Supreme Court, ruling that states cannot make changes to the SC list published under Article 341 of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. The Supreme Court in July 2024 quashed Bihar's 2015 notification that merged Tanti-Tantwa with the SC 'Pan/Sawasi' caste.

questions.question:
[Q.117]
Who won the Men Singles title at the French Open Tennis Tournament 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Carlos Alcaraz won the 2024 French Open men's singles, beating Alexander Zverev.

questions.question:
[Q.118]
Who among the following achieved the distinction of being the first Indian mountaineer to scale Mount Everest and Mount Lhotse twice in one season?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Satyadeep Gupta became the first Indian to climb Everest and Lhotse twice in one season (May 2024).

questions.question:
[Q.119]
What is the sex ratio in Bihar as per the Census 2011 of India?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. According to Census 2011, Bihar's sex ratio is 918 females per 1000 males.

questions.question:
[Q.120]
Which of the following the chlorophyll in photosynthesis is used for?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Chlorophyll's role in photosynthesis is to absorb light energy.

questions.question:
[Q.121]
The political strategy Struggle-Truce-Struggle or S-T-S came into prominence with a call for
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): Deleted. Deleted by BPSC in the final answer key; counts as correct for everyone. Reason given by BPSC: the debate on the S-T-S strategy came up during the Civil Disobedience Movement, so none of the options is correct. (The provisional key had B.)

questions.question:
[Q.122]
During the Quit India Movement parallel 'National Government' was established at many places. Which of the following is not correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The parallel governments were Prati Sarkar (Satara), Jatiya Sarkar (Tamluk) and the Talcher movement (Odisha); there was no 'Raiyati Sarkar' at Kheda, so A is wrongly matched.

questions.question:
[Q.123]
Which of the following is equivalent to tesla?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. From F = BIL, 1 tesla = 1 newton per ampere-metre (N A⁻¹ m⁻¹).

questions.question:
[Q.124]
Which dynasty ruled Magadh (Bihar) after Shishunag dynasty?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. The Nanda dynasty followed the Shishunagas in Magadha.

questions.question:
[Q.125]
Among the following who has been Speaker of Lok Sabha prior to his Election as President of India?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was Lok Sabha Speaker before he became President in 1977.

questions.question:
[Q.126]
When did Bihar State introduce the Green Budget for the first time?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Bihar presented its first Green Budget in FY 2020-21.

questions.question:
[Q.127]
Manvi Madhu Kashyap recently became Bihar's first transgender
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Manvi Madhu Kashyap became Bihar's first transgender Sub-Inspector of Police in 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.128]
Which of the following is a zaid crop?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Fodder crops are grown in the short zaid season (between rabi and kharif); gram and mustard are rabi crops and cotton is kharif.

questions.question:
[Q.129]
Shreyasi Singh, Member of the Legislative Assembly, who has represented India in shooting in Paris Olympics 2024 was elected from which constituency in Bihar?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Shooter Shreyasi Singh won the Jamui Assembly seat in 2020 and competed in trap shooting at the Paris 2024 Olympics.

questions.question:
[Q.130]
What was the chief economic foundation of the triangular commerce between India, China and England?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Opium grown in India was sold in China to pay for tea exported to England; opium was the basis of the triangular trade.

questions.question:
[Q.131]
Which of the following is full form of PCRA?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. PCRA stands for Petroleum Conservation Research Association.

questions.question:
[Q.132]
In October 1943, Subhash Chandra Bose set up a provisional government of free India which was recognized by how many countries including Japan?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The Azad Hind provisional government (October 1943) was recognised by nine Axis-aligned countries, including Japan.

questions.question:
[Q.133]
What is the title of the film by Payal Kapadia for which she became the first Indian filmmaker to win the Grand Prix Award at the Cannes Film Festival in May 2024?
options: The Man Who Could Not Remain Silent
Sunflowers Were the First Ones to Know
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Payal Kapadia's 'All We Imagine as Light' won the Grand Prix at Cannes 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.134]
Which part of alimentary canal receives bile from the liver?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Bile from the liver (stored in the gall bladder) enters the duodenum, the first part of the small intestine.

questions.question:
[Q.135]
Indian National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on which date?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag on 22 July 1947.

questions.question:
[Q.136]
Size of Council of Ministers has been restricted to 15 percent of membership of Lok Sabha by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. The 91st Amendment (2003) capped the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha's (or Assembly's) strength.

questions.question:
[Q.137]
Who is the winner of the prestigious Goldman Environmental Prize 2024 from the region of Asia?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Alok Shukla of Chhattisgarh won the 2024 Goldman Environmental Prize for Asia for protecting the Hasdeo Arand forests.

questions.question:
[Q.138]
Under the Royal Titles Act, Queen Victoria became the empress of India in
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Under the Royal Titles Act 1876, Queen Victoria was proclaimed Empress of India at the Delhi Durbar of 1 January 1877.

questions.question:
[Q.139]
Which of the following pairs will give displacement reactions?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Copper is more reactive than silver, so it displaces silver from AgNO3 solution.

questions.question:
[Q.140]
The Andes extends along which of the following?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. The Andes run along the west coast of South America.

questions.question:
[Q.141]
By which time Governor has to return an ordinary bill to the concerned State Legislature for reconsideration?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Article 200 sets no time limit within which the Governor must return a bill (other than a money bill) for reconsideration.

questions.question:
[Q.142]
What is the current profession of the young U. P. Woman, Arti, who was conferred the Amal Clooney Women's Empowerment Award by the King Charles III in May 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. Arti, a young woman from UP who drives an e-rickshaw, received the Amal Clooney Women's Empowerment Award from the British Asian Trust in 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.143]
The process of breaking down organic matter by micro organisms is called
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): C. Decomposition is the breakdown of organic matter by microorganisms (decomposers).

questions.question:
[Q.144]
Who among the following Indian capitalist was not the architect of "Bombay Plan"?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. The Bombay Plan (1944) was drafted by J. R. D. Tata, G. D. Birla, Lala Shri Ram and others; Dhirubhai Ambani was not among them.

questions.question:
[Q.145]
Which country became the first to bring soil from the dark side of the moon in June 2024?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. China's Chang'e-6 returned the first samples from the far side of the Moon in June 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.146]
What is the name of the one month long cattle fair organized at the confluence of Ganga and Gandak rivers?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. The Sonepur (Harihar Kshetra) cattle fair is held at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak.

questions.question:
[Q.147]
Who decides the disqualification of members of State Legislative Assembly, for matters other than those in the tenth schedule of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. Under Article 192, questions of disqualification (other than under the Tenth Schedule) are decided by the Governor on the opinion of the Election Commission.

questions.question:
[Q.148]
Which of the following is a major cause of air pollution?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): B. Burning of fossil fuels in vehicles, industry and power plants is the major cause of air pollution.

questions.question:
[Q.149]
Munger Hilly region is a part of which of the following physiographic region?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): A. According to the official key, the Munger hills belong to the Southern Hilly Region of Bihar.

questions.question:
[Q.150]
Who was the first one to propose a model for the structure of an atom?
questions.explanation: Official BPSC final answer key (Set G): D. J. J. Thomson proposed the first atomic model (the 'plum pudding' model) in 1904.
